_comment: Manually authored per-image, per-variant layout. Every crop and text position here was chosen by gridding/cropping that specific photo and measuring its actual negative space and product/model boundaries — nothing is computed by the renderer. `crop` is {x,y,width,height} in the ORIGINAL MASTER's pixel coordinates (a lossless sharp .extract(), never a resize/distort — width/height are always exactly 4:5). All other coordinates (textBox, supportPosition, dividerPosition, brandPosition) are in the CROPPED canvas's own coordinates (top-left of the crop = 0,0), since that crop is the actual output canvas. A variant may set headlineLinesOverride/accentLineIndexOverride to test a different line-break of the SAME assigned copy from copy.json (not different words).

MOL_IMG_001._photo_notes: REVISED round 2: round-1 variants kept the crop's right edge at the original x1122 the whole time because the product's right boundary was mismeasured (assumed ~x1090-1100). Re-measured precisely this round: the socks actually end at x~1005. That freed ~85-90px of previously-unused margin on the right — this round's 'product still too small' fix comes from trimming the crop's right edge down to x1035-1090 (25-55px of real margin past the sock, not 120px of empty rug/table it had before). Text zone is the same out-of-focus curtain strip at top-right, now measured against each variant's own (tighter) right edge, which is why headline size shrinks a bit as the crop tightens (V1 69px -> V3 56px): trading zone width for product prominence, which is what was asked for.
MOL_IMG_001._final_en_notes: FINAL EN SET — TEMPLATE_BOTTOM. Sideboard (left) and coffee table (right) span nearly the full frame, so a narrow side panel would crop into one or the other; the full-width top-crop keeps the whole scene (sideboard, her, table with mug/bowl) intact and lets the cream band below hold the headline at full size.

MOL_IMG_005._photo_notes: REPLACED — new copy ('Simple care'/'fits right'/'in.'), rebuilt from scratch on the current locked design system (135px single rigid headline block, no per-line gaps) rather than the old 74px cabinet-strip layout from many rounds ago. Full master used as canvas (no crop, unlike the old version's 1080x1350 crop). Her face runs from hair-bun-top ~y30 to chin ~y300 (head/hair x-range ~450-680); she's chopping vegetables with both hands on a knife at ~x580-750,y480-650. Y=310 puts the block's real ink at 280.8-708.9: clears her chin (10px+), and line 1 (the only line wide enough to reach the hand's x-range) ends its ink at ~437 — well above the hand's y480 start, so no line crosses it. Support/divider/brand follow at y710+, and (support's widest at 648px) still stay ~480px clear of the knife/hands and 380px+ clear of the socks (~x350-480,y1190+).
MOL_IMG_005._template_test_notes: TEST ONLY (pivot to templates A/B/C) — templateA/templateC added this round. B skipped: this photo has no genuinely clean negative space (she + counter + produce span nearly the full frame), so forcing a full-image overlay here is exactly the failure mode the pivot is meant to eliminate. photoCrop x=250 (of the 1122-wide master) keeps her fully inside the 673px photo panel (body spans ~x360-840) while cropping only the left shelving and a sliver of the right-edge basil pot. Template A's 339px-wide cream column caps the headline at 64px (width-bound, not a face/hand workaround — this is simply what a 40%-wide panel allows); the support line ('Wear MOLOSOC while real life keeps moving.') doesn't fit even at 16px in that column, so it's wrapped via supportLinesOverride into 'Wear MOLOSOC while' / 'real life keeps moving.', unchanged words. Template C's photoCrop is the master's top 939px (y0) for all three test images, uncropped horizontally; its wider, shorter cream band supports 93px (height-bound instead of width-bound, and constrained by needing room below the headline for support/divider/brand, not by headline width alone — an earlier width-only estimate of ~125px was wrong because it ignored that shared budget).

MOL_IMG_019._photo_notes: Approved as-is this round — unchanged from the prior round. Standing, watering plants. Head ~y40, product (socks) ~x530-870,y1150-1300. Crop trims only the right side (chair/window); the large plain-wall zone top-left (x55-485,y55+) is untouched by the trim, so text layout is identical across variants — the variation here is purely crop tightness/product prominence.
MOL_IMG_019._template_test_notes: TEST ONLY (pivot to templates A/B/C) — templateA/templateB/templateC added this round. This is the one image of the three test subjects with genuinely large clean negative space (the plain wall top-left, confirmed empty from x0-500,y0-~430 before the watering can/hand enter frame), so it's the only one of the three getting a Template B render. templateB reuses the full master (already ~4:5, no crop) with the headline widened to a 480px-wide box (vs the old V1/V2/V3's 430px) since the clean zone extends further right than previously used — headline lands at 92px, essentially the same ceiling as the old approved V1 (84px was already width-bound on 'moves with' at 430px; 92px is what the same word allows once the box is honestly widened to match the real clean span, not a re-measurement of the same box). templateA's photoCrop x=280 keeps her body (~x500-860) and the nearer foreground plants inside the 673px photo panel while trimming the far-left background plants and some right-side window/chair. templateC's photoCrop is the master's top 939px (y0), same as the other two test images, at the same shared 93px headline size for cross-image consistency.

MOL_IMG_012._photo_notes: Standing/kitchen preview (next-3 batch). Full master used as canvas (no crop). Her sleeve/leg sits at a fairly consistent x~300-320 from y340 (arm) down through y700-1100+ (leg), so the left cabinet strip is narrower here than MOL_IMG_005's — textBox width capped at 260 (right edge 315, ~15-25px clear of x300-320) rather than 005's 300, which is why the headline (40px) is smaller than 005's 74px: this photo's own negative space, not a fixed template size. Support wraps 3 ways (same supportLinesOverride mechanism as 005) since the one-line sentence at 28px (442px) is far too wide for this narrower zone.

V2._variant_note: Option A: same 3-line break as V1, headline held at the same safe 40px (her sleeve's soft edge sits ~x285-300 here throughout y370-750 — confirmed against the actual V1 render, not just the photo grid — so 'complicated.' at 40px/230.7px-wide, right edge 285.7, is this zone's real ceiling without risking overlap). What changes is spacing: headlineLineHeight 1.15->1.35 for real breathing room between lines, support/wordmark stepped up (28->30 / 22->24) for clearer hierarchy, and the whole block starts higher (y400->370, right under the shelf) with wider gaps between headline/support/divider/brand so it reads as one deliberate, resolved block instead of a cramped one.

V3._variant_note: Option B: literally stacks the headline across 4 lines ('Simple'/'care.'/'Nothing'/'complicated.') instead of 3, per the 'stack across more lines to make it larger and cleaner' instruction. The width ceiling is unchanged (still bounded by 'complicated.' at 40px, same 285.7px right edge as V1/V2 — no single line was ever wider than that word), but 4 short, generously-spaced lines (lineHeight 1.3) occupy more vertical presence and read as a bolder, more editorial stack than 3 denser lines.

V4._variant_note: Option C: same 3-line headline as V1/V2 at the same safe 40px, but the whole four-part block (headline/support/divider/brand, total height ~366px) is vertically centered within the full clean cabinet run (shelf ends ~y340, her leg/counter don't force a stop until ~y950) rather than pinned right under the shelf — equal breathing room above and below so the block feels deliberately placed in the middle of the negative space, not just dropped at its top edge.

MOL_IMG_018._photo_notes: Relaxed/sofa preview (next-3 batch). Full master used as canvas (no crop). The whole upper-left is clean sheer curtain, but a narrow column (x55-150) stays clean far deeper (past y500) than the wider block does (her hair reaches x180-250 by y390-420) — so the whole 4-part stack (headline/support/divider/brand) is kept inside the fully-clean band above y~380 rather than risking the diagonal hairline, which keeps every size more compact than MOL_IMG_005's: headline 58px, support 20px wrapped 3 ways, wordmark 16px.

MOL_IMG_020._photo_notes: Seated/floor preview (next-3 batch). Full master used as canvas (no crop). Same diagonal-hairline shape as MOL_IMG_018 (she's seated against the sofa, leaning her head down/right onto the book) — headline (60px) fits in the fully-clean band above y~260, but the support line ('Make it part of the moments you already enjoy.' — the longest supporting line of any post so far) would need ~245px+ at any comfortable size, which crosses into her hairline once positioned below the headline. Wrapped into 4 short lines at 22px (widest 144.5px) to stay inside the narrow x55-200 column that stays clean to y~400.

MOL_IMG_002._photo_notes: REVISED again — one rigid 3-line block now (no headlineLineGaps, no per-line repositioning), per the locked-headline rule. Solved by finding a single Y where the WHOLE block's real ink span (which runs from Y-29 to Y+399 at 135px/0.90 — the font's true ascent/descent extends well beyond the nominal line box) clears every obstacle at once: her chin (~y400-410), her hand (~x580-720,y950-1050), and the sock (~x150-350,y900-1000). Y=445 puts the block's ink at 415.8-844.9 — 5px clear of her chin above and, more importantly, ~55px clear of the sock/hand below. Support/divider/brand keep tight but real gaps (12/8/8px) to land at y821.5-895.9, ~4px clear of the sock — the tightest safe margin in this batch, but a real one, not an estimate.
MOL_IMG_002._final_en_notes: FINAL EN SET — TEMPLATE_BOTTOM. Water bottle (far left) and sofa (far right) both frame the activity; a side panel would lose one or the other, so the full-width top-crop keeps the whole scene together.

MOL_IMG_003._photo_notes: REVISED again — one rigid 3-line block, per the locked-headline rule. Her face runs to the very top of frame (chin ~y300) and she holds an open book with both hands at ~x600-780,y480-620; the block's own ink span at Y=310 runs 280.8-708.9 — clears her chin (5-15px) and clears her hands by ~19px (line 1's descender reaches only to ~471, well short of 480). The other two lines are narrow enough ('A little' / 'quiet.') that they don't reach her hands' x-range at all regardless of y. Her feet/sock are further right (~x650+) and never enter this block's horizontal reach. Support/divider/brand follow with normal spacing at y710+, more than 200px clear of the sock (~y960+).
MOL_IMG_003._template_test_notes: TEST ONLY (pivot to templates A/B/C) — templateA/templateC added this round. B skipped: her face/book/hands and legs/socks together span nearly the entire frame (~x240-920 of the 1122-wide master), leaving no genuinely clean zone large enough for the headline without the same face/hand-avoidance problem the pivot exists to solve. photoCrop x=300 keeps her face, book and legs inside the 673px photo panel, trimming only the side table/mug on the far left and a sliver of garden-door glass on the right. Template A's 339px-wide cream column caps the headline at 61px — a width-bound ceiling from the 40%-wide panel itself, not a reduction made to dodge a face or hand. Template C's photoCrop is the master's top 939px (y0), trimming only the lower legs/floor; its wider band supports 93px, sized to leave room below the headline for support/divider/brand rather than to the width limit alone.

MOL_IMG_004._photo_notes: FLAGGED CONFLICT — could not fully satisfy the locked single-rigid-block rule and 'never cover hands' simultaneously for this photo; explaining why rather than silently picking one. Her obstacles stack too densely for a rigid 428px-tall ink block (3 lines at 135px/0.90) to dodge all of them: chin ends ~y260, she's gripping the vacuum with one hand on the canister (~x330-420,y490-570) and one on the handle (~x480-560,y620-720), and her socks start ~y1090. The two hand-free gaps this could sit in are the chin-to-hand gap (260-490, only 230px) and the hand-to-sock gap (720-1090, 370px) — both smaller than the 428px block needs, so no single Y clears the chin, both hands, AND the sock at once. This lays the block at Y=300 (ink 270.8-698.9): it clears her chin (10px) and clears the sock by ~390px, prioritizing the two rules that have mattered most across this whole project (face, then product) — but its own ink does cross both hand grips, which the old per-line-gap version had avoided by routing around them individually. Flagging this rather than either silently shipping the hand overlap or unilaterally overriding the new one-block rule to fix it.
MOL_IMG_004._final_en_notes: FINAL EN SET — TEMPLATE_BOTTOM. The vacuum wand extends diagonally across most of the frame's width (dining table left, sofa right); a narrow side panel would cut the wand or one of the flanking pieces, so the full-width top-crop keeps the whole action intact.

MOL_IMG_006._photo_notes: REVISED again — one rigid 3-line block for the headline itself fits, but flagging a related conflict for the secondary lockup below it. Still shifted to x=160 (sharp-focus framed print at x0-145). Her chin ends ~y300, her hands are on the laptop/desk at ~x550-720,y560-680, and — measured precisely this round, tighter than earlier estimated — her sock starts at ~y1120, not ~y1150. The only gap big enough for the 428px headline block is between her hands and the sock (680-1120, 440px), and it barely fits: Y=715 puts the block's ink at 685.8-1113.9, ~6px clear on both sides. But that leaves only ~40px between the headline and the sock for support+divider+brand to fit 'underneath the headline' as required — physically less than support+divider+brand need even with zero spacing (~58px). Divider (90px wide) is narrow enough it never reaches the sock's x-range, but support and brand do, and can't both be squeezed above y1120: this lockup unavoidably overlaps the top few px of the sock at whatever position it takes. Flagging rather than silently shipping it or unilaterally resizing/detaching the lockup to dodge it.
MOL_IMG_006._final_en_notes: FINAL EN SET — TEMPLATE_SIDE. She's a fairly contained vertical figure leaning over the desk; photoCrop x=280 keeps her plus the laptop/desk/mug inside the 673px photo panel, trimming only the far-left bookshelf and far-right window/lamp. No face/hand-avoidance math needed anymore — text lives entirely in the cream panel, never on the photo.

MOL_IMG_007._photo_notes: REVISED again — same 135px/0.90 typography and same position as the previous round (kept per 'close to current look'): this was already the best-behaved of the five, with line 3 clearing her entirely and only a ~10px graze of the left edge of her hair from line 2 ('Your feet') — a soft hair edge, not her face/hairline proper, so left as-is.
MOL_IMG_007._final_en_notes: FINAL EN SET — TEMPLATE_SIDE. She's seated centrally in the armchair with book+coffee; photoCrop x=250 centers her in the 673px photo panel, trimming the cabinet on the far left and the small side table on the far right. 'Slow down.' is this copy's widest line and caps the headline at 62px in the 335px-wide cream column — a width-bound ceiling from the panel geometry, not a shrink to dodge an obstacle (there is no obstacle to dodge anymore).

MOL_IMG_008._photo_notes: Next-5 batch, current locked design system (135px single rigid block). Full master, no crop. Face runs to chin ~y300-320; she's arranging flowers with both hands at ~x580-750,y400-580 — closer to her chin than in most of this batch, so a single line can't sit between them (only ~80-100px gap vs. ~185px needed). Block instead starts at Y=625, clearing the hands (ink top ~596, 16px past y580) and finishing (ink bottom ~1024) well above the sock (~x330-620,y1140+). Support/divider/brand follow at y1025+, ending ~15px clear of the sock.
MOL_IMG_008._final_en_notes: FINAL EN SET — TEMPLATE_BOTTOM. Dining set (far left) and stove/shelving (far right) both anchor this kitchen scene; the full-width top-crop keeps the whole room intact rather than cropping into either side.

MOL_IMG_009._photo_notes: FLAGGED CONFLICT, same as MOL_IMG_004/006 in the previous round — could not fully avoid her hands while also clearing chin and sock. Her chin ends ~y360, she's applying cream with both hands at ~x400-620,y480-650, and her sock (feet up on the ottoman) starts unusually high at ~y1010 (not ~1150 like most of this set). The three gaps this could sit in — chin-to-hand (360-480, 120px), hand-to-sock (650-1010, 360px) — are both well short of the 428px a rigid 3-line 135px block needs, so no Y clears all three. Placed at Y=600 (ink 570.8-964.4) to clear her chin and the sock, the two rules weighted heaviest elsewhere in this project; the block's own ink does cross her hands. Support/divider/brand (a much shorter line at 30px, only 495px wide) never reach the sock's x-range (650-1050) regardless of y, so they follow with normal spacing and no further conflict.
MOL_IMG_009._final_en_notes: FINAL EN SET — TEMPLATE_BOTTOM (not SIDE): 'Take a moment.' is long enough that it doesn't fit at a large size in the 335px-wide SIDE column (even at 64px it overflows to 456.9px) — forcing SIDE here would mean shrinking this specific headline well below the rest of the set's scale just to make it fit, which the brief explicitly rules out. The wide cream band gives this exact copy the room a large headline needs; textBox widened to 700px (vs. the usual 600px) and headline set to 88px, still fitting comfortably within that band.

MOL_IMG_010._photo_notes: Next-5 batch, current locked design system. Full master, no crop. Face runs to chin ~y230-250; she's writing with both hands at ~x350-500,y400-540. Block starts at Y=585 (ink 555.8-983.9), clearing her hands with margin. None of the 3 headline lines are wide enough to reach the raised sock (~x600-820,y880-1030) — the widest, 'moment', only reaches x558. The support line IS wide enough (edge 641), so it's held at y1040 — in the ~110px gap between the raised sock (ends ~1030) and the other foot's sock (starts ~1140) — rather than following immediately after the headline.
MOL_IMG_010._final_en_notes: FINAL EN SET — TEMPLATE_SIDE. She's seated on the window bench, contained enough for a vertical crop; photoCrop x=250 keeps her and most of the round side table (mug, flowers) inside the 673px photo panel, trimming only the far-left cushion/blanket and the table's far right edge.

MOL_IMG_011._photo_notes: FLAGGED CONFLICT, same shape as MOL_IMG_004/009 — the densest obstacle stack in this batch. Chin ends ~y300; she applies cream in two separate motions, one hand+jar at ~x480-620,y460-580 and the other rubbing it into her leg at ~x400-620,y650-800; her sock appears right after, at ~y900. Three gaps (chin-hand1 160px, hand1-hand2 70px, hand2-sock 100px) are all far short of the 428px block. Placed at Y=400 (ink 370.8-798.9) to clear her chin (70px) and the sock (101px) — the block's own ink crosses both hand positions. Support is pushed to y800 (clearing hand2's tail) and the whole lockup ends ~12px above the sock at y900.
